findings.where: Hero (first screen, both widths): the big arches, the centred capitals 'MARK · M · MOSELEY / INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR' and the line under them
findings.fault: Mark is neither seen nor heard on the first screen. The arches fill the whole hero, and the tile leaves no place where Mark's portrait would sit on the stone. The only sentence is in the third person ('from a former Lead Lawyer…'), under a centred name in carved capitals. The screen reads like a dedication on a monument, not a person speaking. The direction never shows how a real face and Mark's own words would sit in this look.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder. The brief's client values 1 and 3 ask for a personal, approachable advisor who is seen and heard in his own words, and first-visit trust item 1 asks for a real photo of the face. A development-bank officer looking for an individual gets a stone plaque and no person. The layout round will have no way to add Mark's photo within this look.

findings.where: Nav lockup and hero mark (both widths), and the palette as a whole
findings.fault: Mark's logo as he knows it, the arches in grey with a blue 'MMM INFRA' wordmark, appears nowhere. The nav mark and its wordmark are recoloured to the dark 'cut' colour. The hero shows the arches with no wordmark under them, and Cinzel's 'MARK · M · MOSELEY' takes the wordmark's place. So the frame the opening move ends on is a new lockup, not the logo, and the logo's blue is gone from the whole direction.
findings.who_objects: Mark. Client value 7 says the logo stays and the opening animation builds it, and the brief says the mark is never redrawn. He would see his own identity replaced by a new name-under-arches lockup in a colour scheme that leaves out his blue.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the headline 'THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW' and the rule that every heading is in tracked Cinzel capitals
findings.fault: Every heading must be in widely spaced capitals, because Cinzel has no lowercase. The short specimen title already runs to three heavy lines in its column. Mark's real titles run longer: the lecture beside it is 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge'. In this style it would become a block of four or five lines of capitals that dominates the article and is slow to read.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will add posts with whatever titles Mark writes (client value 9, a look that survives a lay editor). A reader in Read mode also has to get through a wall of capitals before reaching the text.

findings.where: Hero heading (desktop especially): 'MARK · M · MOSELEY' over 'INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR'
findings.fault: Both lines are the same size, and the role line is about half as wide again as the name. When you squint, the job title wins over the man's name, and the generic role is what the eye takes first.
findings.who_objects: Mark. The brief says the individual is the brand (client value 1, brand sheet §5), so his name should lead, not the job description.

findings.where: Palette tile: the four equal swatches GRANITE, CUT, MINIUM, LIME (the LIME swatch is a second red block with 'AA')
findings.fault: Four blocks of equal size, two of them solid red, make red look like half the palette. In fact granite is the whole ground and minium is only the one button. The tile shows the colours at equal weight and gives the opposite of the direction's 'one accent only' idea.
findings.who_objects: The layout round's designer, who builds from this tile and could read red as a main surface colour. The brief's guardrail also bans 'several colours at equal weight'.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel: the note under the timeline table ('#13, docs/research/animation-length.md F5/F12') and the 'units (≈290 px)' figures
findings.fault: Internal ticket numbers and a repository file path in monospace sit in a tile that is shown to the client. Here working notes take the place of the brand's voice.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who will be shown this tile on #10. Those references mean nothing to him and make the direction read as an engineering document rather than his site's look.

findings.where: Texture tile: the large carved 'M' centred in the ashlar courses
findings.fault: A single large capital set in its own stone block reads as a monogram, which is a second brand mark beside the arches logo. A designer drawing from this tile could carry the 'M' seal forward as an identity element.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder. Client value 7 keeps the existing logo as the one mark, and a new monogram competes with it.
